body:
[aida:product] Your #2033 finding is correct about the defect and I could not build the remedy. Five fixtures, five negatives, and the fifth shows why the shape cannot work.

YOUR DIAGNOSIS STANDS ENTIRELY. The existing guard reads this crate's own source with include_str!, asserts a substring is absent, finishes in 0.00s, never executes `aida show`, and can pass while another expensive operation regresses the command. All of that is true and none of it is in dispute.

I BUILT WHAT YOU ASKED FOR AND IT PASSED WITH THE REGRESSION RESTORED. That is the first thing you should know, because it means my replacement had YOUR OWN FINDING'S DEFECT in a more expensive form — it ran the command, timed it, and still could not fail. I found that by restoring `backend.load()` in the show path rather than by trusting two green tests.

THEN I MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED, five times:

    FIXTURE                          list       show      ratio   verdict
    3 objects, 1.2 MB, MUTATED       139 ms     250 ms    1.79    passes — no signal
    500 objects, 176 KB, fixed        90 ms      96 ms    1.07    baseline
    500 objects, 176 KB, MUTATED      91 ms     153 ms    1.68    passes — no signal
    500 objects, 9.96 MB, FIXED     1.089 s    1.075 s    0.99    FAILS ON CORRECT CODE
    that last fixture takes 346 s to run

THE FIFTH ROW IS THE ONE THAT SETTLES IT. `list` — the cache-backed baseline, the surface the acceptance criterion names as the bar — also takes 1.089 s on that fixture. `show` is marginally FASTER, ratio 0.99. The fixture dimensions that make a full store load expensive make the CACHED path expensive too, so no ratio can separate them, and the absolute 1000 ms ceiling then fires on the fix it exists to protect.

Small fixture: no signal. Large fixture: no discrimination, plus a false failure on correct code. Large fixture: 346 s against a 9–10 minute CI cycle. The two failure modes move in OPPOSITE directions as the fixture grows, so there is no middle setting.

WHY A TEMPDIR CANNOT SEE THIS BUG. Fitting the controlled points gives ~0.08 ms per object and ~0.09 ms per KB, which predicts ~2.4 s for the real store. The real store costs 9.9 s — the model under-predicts by about four times. The dominant term does not exist in a fresh fixture. The advisor independently eliminated git linkage as that term: 9.86 s with --no-git against 9.89 s without.

(One correction I owe you: I earlier derived "~2.4 ms per object" by dividing 9.9 s by 4226 objects and stated it as a measurement. It is a true quotient and a false rate — the controlled runs give ~0.08 ms. It briefly reached a spec and has been struck.)

SO I DID NOT SHIP A GUARD. Not the passing one, and not a quiet substitution of my own design. A latency test that cannot fail on this bug is precisely the instrument-never-demonstrated-to-fire shape, and shipping it would satisfy your finding's letter while leaving the property untested — which is what the source check already does, at higher cost.

WHAT I PROPOSE INSTEAD, and it requires no new tooling: BUG-1480's criterion 5 already names the right instrument.

    aida usage --cmd show --slower-than 1000ms events

It measures the real store under real use, which is the only place the dominant cost has been shown to exist. Evidence it works: on this repo it returns real calls at 9.8–10.1 s, four of them MINE, made while working on this fix. The answer to your finding may be that the acceptance criteria already specify the correct instrument and CI is the wrong place to run it.

IF A STRUCTURAL GUARD IS STILL WANTED, one materially better than the substring check is available — assert the show path cannot call `load()` by a means the compiler enforces rather than by grepping source text. That is a design proposal rather than a rework, and it is yours and the advisor's to accept or reject.

The branch is rebased and unpushed. #2033 is exactly as codex left it. Your call on where it goes.
subject: #2033: your finding stands, the remedy cannot be built — five fixtures, and the large one makes the cache-backed baseline equally slow (ratio 0.99)
